description: Single-panel figure: a secondary-electron SEM micrograph of the Fe–Mn–Al–C alloy 12Al-20Mn-1C tempered at 800 °C, acquired at 20 kV with nominal magnification X5,000; the instrument parameters "20kV X5,000" and a 5 µm scale bar are printed along the bottom edge, and no panel letters, axes or legend are present. No numeric composition or property values are printed anywhere in the field. The image is dominated by wide, thick, lath-like lamellae of bright contrast (the κ-carbide strips named in the text) set in a darker matrix; the laths run in several orientations — long parallel bands in the lower and central areas, and branching/stepped bundles to the right — with small dark elongated pits or pulled-out particles aligned inside them. The upper-left corner is a brighter region carrying a fine cross-hatched, modulated texture. Read together with Fig. 5(c) and Table 7, the panel demonstrates that the fully austenitically decomposed 800 °C structure is a coarse lamellar κ-carbide + austenite (residual-γ) arrangement formed by cellular transformation plus spinodal decomposition, with lamellae visibly wider and thicker than in 9Al-10Mn-1C.

subfigures.description: Secondary-electron SEM micrograph, 20 kV, X5,000, 5 µm scale bar: wide thick lath-like bright lamellae in a darker matrix, lamellae in several orientations with small dark elongated pits inside them; a brighter upper-left region shows a fine cross-hatched modulated texture.

observations.observation: The micrograph is a secondary-electron SEM image recorded at 20 kV with nominal magnification X5,000, with a 5 µm scale bar printed at the bottom of the field.

The dominant feature is wide, thick, lath-like lamellae of bright contrast embedded in a darker matrix, running in multiple orientations and forming long parallel bands as well as branching/stepped bundles.
Small dark, elongated pits or pulled-out particles are aligned within and along the lamellae.

The upper-left corner of the field is a brighter region with a fine cross-hatched (modulated) texture, distinct from the lamellar area; its crystallographic identity is not determinable from the image alone.
No axes, legends, data labels or numeric property values are printed; the only readable annotations are '20kV', 'X5,000' and '5µm'.
The caption states the figure shows lamellae in 12Al-20Mn-1C at 800 °C.

The phase symbols in the caption are corrupted in the supplied text (' + Lamellae'), so the exact phase names attached to the lamellae (κ-carbide and austenite/residual-γ) are inferred from the citing text, not from the caption string itself.
The citing text states that these κ-carbides differ from those at lower Al because they consist of wide, thick lath-like lamellae.
The citing text states that at 12% aluminium the κ-carbide lath-like strips look wider and thicker than at 9% Al.

The citing text states that the 800 °C tempered 12Al-20Mn-1C alloy underwent full austenitic decomposition via cellular transformation into κ-carbide + γ + residual-γ lamellar structures together with spinodal decomposition.
The citing text states that, because of the wide lamellae, EDS analysis of this condition was more accurate (reported in Table 7).
The citing text notes that even though the inter-lamellar spacing is high for this condition, the hardening effects remained consistent (Table 5).

measured_quantities: lamella width/thickness (µm) — imaged but not quantified on the panel
inter-lamellar spacing (µm) — discussed in text, not measured on the panel
